  1. aspect 1 0 0 1 main= 1 0 <0 1 0

Grok's response (as captured)

The message was read as (or partly as) a 3×33 \times 33×3 identity matrix:

I3=(100010001)I_3 = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{pmatrix}I3​=​100​010​001​​

(the "<0" was taken as a shift error for a row ending in 0 / 0 1).

Key properties:

  • Multiplication: I⋅A=A⋅I=AI \cdot A = A \cdot I = AI⋅A=A⋅I=A for any compatible matrix AAA.
  • Determinant: det⁡(I)=1\det(I) = 1det(I)=1.
  • Inverse: I−1=II^{-1} = II−1=I.
  • Eigenvalues: all 111, with eigenvectors along the standard basis ⟨1,0,0⟩\langle 1,0,0\rangle⟨1,0,0⟩, ⟨0,1,0⟩\langle 0,1,0\rangle⟨0,1,0⟩, ⟨0,0,1⟩\langle 0,0,1\rangle⟨0,0,1⟩.

Grok noted "aspect" likely refers to aspect ratio in graphics (e.g., scaling xxx vs. yyy in a projection matrix), where the identity preserves 1:1 scaling with no distortion. It asked for clarification because the message was garbled.
